text:
Dmitry Orlov won a Stanley Cup in Washington, has nearly 1,000 NHL games behind him, and at 35 told Sharks Hockey Digest he's "not really happy" with his start. That's an honest read on a hard month: San Jose has taken only 40% of the expected goals with him on the ice, about four points worse than without him, and his minutes have dropped by two a night over his last ten games.

The points have held up, mostly through the power play. He has nine points in 19 games, six of them with the man advantage, including two power-play assists last week. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says he's still hard to beat at his own blue line, stopping 15% of the entries aimed at him against a typical 11%.

He's also scoring at a rate he won't keep: his shooting percentage (11.8%) is about double what defensemen settle at. Evolving-Hockey had him near replacement level last season, with the power play doing most of the work. Our range has him at 25 to 40 points over a full season. His role is the veteran on the second power-play unit and a steady partner for whoever the Sharks develop next to him.
headline: Orlov is not happy, and says so
